prs.title: refactor(ast)!: migrate string literals and templates to JSStr
fix(ast)!: preserve lone surrogates in static member names
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
`obj["\uD800"]` has a static property name, but after #26548 the member-name helpers return `None` for it because the name is not valid UTF-8. Consumers then treat the member as dynamic.

`static_property_name()` and `static_property_info()` now return the name as a borrowed `JSStr`. This fixes lone-surrogate names in `no-self-assign`, `no-console`, React `displayName` inference, and enum member references in declaration output.

## Breaking changes

- `static_property_name()` and `static_property_info()` on the member expression types return `JSStr<'a>` instead of `&'a str` / `Str<'a>`. Use `as_str()` where UTF-8 is required.

`PropertyKey` and class element names are handled in #27095.

Based on #26548. Part of #26242.

Implemented with AI assistance.

prs.title: fix(minifier): preserve indirect access when folding into call targets
prs.author: waltuov
prs.body:
Part of #24331.

When the minifier folds something into a call target, it can drop the `(0, x)` form. That changes `this` for member calls and turns an indirect `eval` into a direct one. The tracker lists the optional chain case:

```js
(function(o) { console.log((0, o?.f)(42)); })({ a: "PASS", f(b) { return this.a || b; } });
// minified: (e?.f)(42), prints PASS instead of 42
```

Checking the other places that move an expression into a call target or tag found three more paths with the same problem:

```js
// IIFE body substitution
(() => o.f)()();       // -> o.f()
delete (() => o.f)();  // -> delete o.f

// unused assignment removal (identifier and member targets)
let t; (t = o.f)();    // -> o.f()
let t; (t = eval)(x);  // -> eval(x), a direct eval

// single use inlining into a tag
let c = a.b; c``;      // -> a.b``
```

In a debug build, `(t = eval)(x)` and `(() => eval)()(x)` already trip the `stale direct-eval flags` assertion on main.

Changes:
- `should_keep_indirect_access` treats an optional chain that ends in a member access like a plain member access, as the `delete` arm already does.
- A new `preserve_indirect_access_if_needed` helper is used by the IIFE body substitution and both unused assignment removals.
- Single use inlining into a tag wraps a member or member chain replacement as `(0, a.b)`. This is what the two commented out tests in `esbuild.rs` expect, so they are enabled again.

prs.title: fix(ecmascript): do not fold Number.isInteger / isSafeInteger of tiny non-integers to true
prs.author: baltasarblanco
prs.body:
### Bug

```js
console.log(Number.isInteger(5e-324), Number.isSafeInteger(5e-324), Number.isInteger(1e-300), Number.isSafeInteger(-1e-20));
// before: console.log(!0,!0,!0,!0)   -> true true true true
// after:  console.log(!1,!1,!1,!1)   -> false false false false
```

(oxc-minify 0.153.0, default options; same output on `main` at 9a9eb83.) Also through a constant (`const x = 5e-324; Number.isInteger(x)` → `!0`).

It also changes control flow:

```js
var i = setImmediate(function () { console.log("ran"); });
if (Number.isInteger(5e-324)) clearImmediate(i);
```

minifies to ``var e=setImmediate(function(){console.log(`ran`)});clearImmediate(e);``: the original prints `ran`, the minified prints nothing.

`try_fold_number_methods` (`crates/oxc_ecmascript/src/constant_evaluation/call_expr.rs`) tests `extracted.fract().abs() < f64::EPSILON`. `f64::EPSILON` is about `2.2e-16`, so every number with a smaller fractional part counts as an integer. [`Number.isInteger`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-number.isinteger) and [`Number.isSafeInteger`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-number.issafeinteger) only accept an [integral Number](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#integral-number): "a finite Number value whose mathematical value is in the set of integers". That is an exact check.

### Fix

`is_integral = n.is_finite() && n.trunc() == n`, used by both methods.

fix(ast)!: preserve lone surrogates in static property names
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
`PropertyKey::static_name()` and `ClassElement::static_name()` returned `None` for a key such as `{ "\uD800": 1 }`, so rules treated it as dynamic and missed duplicate keys, duplicate class members, accessor pairs and overloads with these names.

They now return `StaticPropertyName`, which borrows the key's `JSStr` from the AST or owns the text of a numeric key. Regex keys use their canonical name, so `[/a/ig]` is `/a/gi`. `sort-keys` now sorts lone-surrogate keys too, with the comparator from #27579. async-to-generator no longer emits an invalid function name such as `1` for a key like `"\uD8001"`. `JSStr::display()` is added for diagnostics; it writes a lone surrogate as `\uXXXX`.

## Breaking changes

- `PropertyKey::static_name`, `PropertyKey::name` and `ClassElement::static_name` return `Option<StaticPropertyName<'a>>` instead of `Option<Cow<'a, str>>`.
- `oxc_semantic::class::table::Element.name` is `StaticPropertyName<'a>`.

Based on #26677. Part of #26242. Continues #26720.

Implemented with AI assistance.

prs.title: fix(ecmascript): correct parseFloat decimal prefix scanning
prs.author: camc314
prs.body: Correct `parseFloat` constant folding to stop at numeric separators and accept an exponent after a decimal point without fractional digits. `parseFloat('1_2')` now folds to `1` instead of `12`, `parseFloat('1e2_3')` to `100` instead of `1e23`, and `parseFloat('1.e2')` to `100` instead of `1`.

prs.title: fix(linter/eslint/no-var): avoid fixes for redeclared bindings
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Skip `no-var` fixes when any binding in the declaration has multiple declarations, matching ESLint's redeclaration guard. This keeps valid repeated `var` declarations from becoming duplicate `const` or `let` declarations while still reporting each violation.

Add regressions for repeated declarations, destructuring, and parameter/function collisions, plus a case confirming that separate scopes remain fixable.

Fixes #27694

prs.title: fix(oxlint,oxfmt): correct Node.js TypeScript support range
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
TypeScript config load errors currently advertise `^20.19.0 || >=22.18.0`, even though Node 20 cannot load TypeScript files natively. Remove the Node 20 range from the shared Oxlint/Oxfmt diagnostic and the matching TypeScript plugin documentation, including generated schema, declarations, and website snapshot. Package engine requirements stay the same.

Fixes #27678

prs.title: fix(linter/unicorn/catch-error-name): avoid fix symbol name collisions
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
`unicorn/catch-error-name` could rename a parameter to an existing binding, producing invalid syntax or capturing another variable. The fixer now appends underscores until the configured name is available in the parameter's scope and every scope where it is referenced, and avoids capturing unresolved references in its body. Diagnostics show the selected name.

Adds regressions for both reported examples, unused catch parameters, nested references, globals, promise callbacks, configured names, and repeated suffix collisions. Generated names are also accepted when the configured name already ends in an underscore.

Fixes #27700.

prs.title: fix(coverage): pin the V8 test262 status list to Node's V8 version
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
monitor-oxc's Test262 job fails on every run because `cargo coverage runtime` no longer matches `runtime.snap`. The runtime suite skips the cases V8's `test262.status` lists as failing, and it fetches that file from V8's `main` branch at run time. On 2026-10-09 V8 landed `03af3c3548` ("[scopes] Reject var arguments in parameter eval") and removed the 88 `language/eval-code/direct/*declare-arguments*` entries. Node 26.5 bundles V8 14.6.202, which predates that fix, so those 88 cases now run and fail with `Expected a SyntaxError to be thrown`.

The skip list exists to hide bugs of the engine that executes the cases, and that engine is Node's V8, not V8 `main`. `main` is wrong in both directions: it un-skips cases V8 fixed after Node's branch cut, and it skips 236 entries for test262 files newer than the pinned checkout.

The list is now fetched at the V8 version reported by `node -p process.versions.v8` (`14.6.202.34`, which V8 tags on GitHub), falling back to `main` only when that tag does not exist. The gitignored cache file carries the version in its name so a Node bump cannot serve a stale list.

With the pinned list the snapshot only changes when the test262 pin or `.node-version` moves. Regenerated against Node 26.5.0 it adds nothing and drops: four `delete/super-property-uninitialized-this` cases that V8 fixed upstream after 14.6, the `typeof/symbol.js` timeout, and the two `bigint-and-number-extremes` minify cases that #27656 fixed (the regular CI does not run the runti

fix(linter/unicorn/consistent-function-scoping): count self-referencing variables as captures
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Treat a function's reference to its own variable binding as a parent-scope capture, matching eslint-plugin-unicorn. For example, a nested `const builder = (...args) => builder.apply(null, args)` was incorrectly reported as movable even though it captures `builder` from the enclosing scope.

Limit the recursion exemption to function-name symbols. Add regression cases for arrow functions, anonymous and named function expressions, parameter defaults, and `var` bindings, while retaining warnings for internal function-name recursion and shadowed parameters.

Addresses report 5 (`unicorn/consistent-function-scoping`) in #27710.

prs.title: fix(linter/eslint/no-div-regex): report quantified leading equals
prs.author: ozenyunus35
prs.body:
The first parsed term in `/=+$/`, `/=*x/`, and `/={2}/` is a quantifier, so these literals were missed. Inspect the quantifier's body to report them consistently with ESLint. The existing autofix still replaces only the leading `=`, turning `/=+$/` into `/[=]+$/`.

Adds regression coverage for quantified leading equals, autofixes, character classes, and non-leading equals.

Part of #27710 (item 2: `eslint/no-div-regex`).

prs.title: fix(linter/eslint/no-magic-numbers): restrict unary exemptions to numeric signs
prs.author: ozenyunus35
prs.body:
Member assignments such as `exports.a = void 0` and `exports.b = ~5` now report the numeric literals, matching ESLint. Only unary `-` and `+` are treated as part of a number, so assignments such as `exports.c = -7` remain allowed.

Adds regression coverage for `void`, `~`, `!`, and `typeof`, plus allowed signed literals.

Addresses #27710, item 4 (`eslint/no-magic-numbers`).

AI assistance was used in preparing this change.

prs.title: fix(linter/eslint/id-length): check destructuring assignment targets
prs.author: ozenyunus35
prs.body:
`id-length` missed identifiers used as destructuring assignment targets, including `[q] = values` and `for ([ix, s] of values) {}`. Check array and object targets, defaults, and rest elements, matching ESLint 10.12.0.

Preserve `properties: "never"` exemptions and report the key when an explicit object property's key and target share a name, including parenthesized computed keys. Regression tests cover assignment targets, exempt reads, and diagnostic locations.

Part of #27710 (report 3).

prs.title: fix(linter/eslint/no-setter-return): check setters in property descriptors
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Oxlint currently allows descriptor setters such as `Object.defineProperty(o, "x", { set: value => value })`, while ESLint reports the returned value.

Recognize setters passed to `Object.defineProperty`, `Reflect.defineProperty`, `Object.defineProperties`, and `Object.create`, including concise arrows. Check argument positions and global bindings, preserve nested-function boundaries, and enable the upstream descriptor tests with additional regression coverage.

Addresses report 1 (`eslint/no-setter-return`) in #27710.

prs.title: fix(linter/eslint/no-useless-assignment): report dead stores to function parameters
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Track function parameter bindings so `function f(p) { p = 5; p = 6; return p; }` reports `p = 5`, matching ESLint. This also covers defaulted, destructured, and rest parameters.

Keep writes during parameter initialization excluded: the CFG does not model skipped defaults or their destructuring evaluation order reliably. Reads in defaults still count as uses.

Fixes #27720

prs.title: refactor(linter): move inline AST paths into imports
fix(linter/eslint/max-params): count rest parameters
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Count rest parameters toward the limit for functions, arrows, and TypeScript function types, matching ESLint. For example, `function f(a, b, c, ...rest) {}` now reports four parameters with the default maximum of three.

Addresses report 12 (`eslint/max-params`) in #27746.

prs.title: fix(linter/unicorn/no-array-callback-reference): ignore callback factory calls
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Match Unicorn by ignoring call expressions passed as callbacks, including `arr.forEach(make(x))` and `arr.map(make(x))`. Suggesting an arrow wrapper would run the factory once per element instead of once per array method call.

Addresses report 4 (`unicorn/no-array-callback-reference`) in #27746.

prs.title: fix(linter/unicorn/catch-error-name): check unused underscore-prefixed names
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Match Unicorn by exempting only the exact unused name `_`. Unused `_err` and `__` are now reported and renamed in catch clauses and promise rejection handlers. Regression tests preserve the `_` exemption and configured names/ignore patterns.

Addresses report 15 (`unicorn/catch-error-name`) in #27746.

prs.title: fix(linter/unicorn/prefer-type-error): handle parenthesized type checks
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Unwrap parentheses when identifying type checks so `!(x instanceof Y)` and `!(typeof x === "string")` report `throw new Error(...)` and fix it to `TypeError`, matching Unicorn. Includes regressions for nested conditions and both autofixes.

Addresses report 16 (`unicorn/prefer-type-error`) in #27746.
